subject: Invoice payment options for multi-entity billing — single-sweep vs per-entity routing

Subject: Invoice 4207 — payment routing question

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We received Invoice #4207 (attached) that covers services consumed across three of our business entities in EMEA and the UK. The invoice lists amounts in EUR, GBP and USD. We're trying to consolidate payments into a single outbound wire from our treasury team to simplify FX, but need to understand how Redwood wants to treat:

- allocation to the three legal entities (how you map a single incoming USD sweep to the per-entity ledger)
- intermediary/correspondent bank fees (who absorbs these?)
- VAT holdback and reclaim instructions for the EUR/UK lines

Our treasury prefers a single USD sweep to your USD account and then Redwood performs the internal allocation. Will Redwood accept that and (a) confirm whether you will net any correspondent fees or (b) require us to send fees separately? Also, if you can confirm the exact remittance reference format we should include, that helps automation on our side.

Attaching invoice file.

Cheers,
Alex Turner
Head of Finance Ops
Northbridge Analytics

Hi Alex — good question, thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: we can support a single USD sweep, but there are two operational paths and different fee/tax implications. Below I've outlined options and the info we need from your side.

Option A — Single USD sweep (preferred by you)
- You wire a single USD payment to our centralized Redwood USD collection account (instructions attached: RW-USD-SWEEP-Instructions.pdf).
- We internally allocate amounts to the three legal entities and post to the correct invoices/ledgers.
- Correspondent/intermediary fees: by default these are charged by the banking chain and our standard policy is "sender pays" (i.e., our bank will expect full beneficiary amount). If your bank sends "OUR" vs "SHA" vs "BEN" differently that will determine who bears fees.
- If you'd like Redwood to absorb correspondent fees, we can do a capped concession (see finance below) but we need explicit confirmation and will either (i) net the capped amount across the posted invoice(s) if fees exceed the cap, or (ii) issue a credit.

Option B — Per-entity receipts (cleanest for tax/VAT)
- You send three wires to entity-specific IBANs (EUR entity, GBP entity, USD entity).
- No internal FX or allocation required; VAT handling is direct on the receiving entity.

What we need from Northbridge to proceed with Option A (single sweep):
1) Clear instruction that this payment is ONE-SWEEP, and a breakdown file showing mapping (invoice lines -> legal entity). We prefer CSV with invoice_line_id, amount, currency, entity_code.
2) Confirmation of which payment instruction type your bank will send (OUR/ SHA/ BEN).
3) Treasury contact and expected payment date so we can book for FX profiling.

Remittance reference (please include exactly): NB-4207 | NB-TREASURY-REF-<your ref>

Looping in Laura and Marissa from Billing/Payments to confirm the collection account and discuss fee concession thresholds.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom — we'll aim for Option A (single USD sweep). A couple of follow-ups:

1) VAT / holdback: Our tax team wants to hold back the EUR VAT amount (we expect to reclaim it). Does Redwood require VAT to be paid gross to the EUR entity in order to support reclaim, or can Redwood process the reclaim on the consolidated payment?

2) Intermediary fees cap: Northbridge can ask our bank to send "OUR" instructions but there are often intermediary bank deductions. Would Redwood consider absorbing intermediary/corridor fees up to a small cap (we propose USD 50 per wire) for this one-time consolidation? If accepted, we will reference that in our treasury note.

3) Final confirmation: we will schedule the sweep for Friday 2028-06-04 if we get confirmation by EOD Thursday.

Appreciate the help — please confirm and provide any acceptance template you need signed.

Best,
Alex

Alex — looping in Rafael (Finance) to confirm concession policy and Laura for VAT process. Quick answers:

1) VAT / holdback: For EU VAT lines we need either (A) the amount to reach the local EU legal entity (Option B), or (B) if you do a centralized USD sweep we will still process the VAT lines for reclaim but we require: the original invoice line IDs, your VAT registration number, and a signed certificate that you will claim the VAT (reverse charge) where applicable. If you want Redwood to act as the reclaiming agent that needs a formal tax engagement and has a lead time.

2) Intermediary fees cap: Finance policy is conservative. We can accept covering intermediary fees up to USD 30 per incoming wire for first-time transactions under a negotiated concession. Anything above USD 30 would be netted against the invoice or invoiced back. Rafael — can you confirm the exact wording we should send to Northbridge for acceptance?

3) Acceptance template: attached is a short finance acceptance letter template we can populate and sign once Northbridge confirms the arrangement (see attached).

If you confirm the single sweep with the remittance reference NB-4207 | NB-TREASURY-REF-XYZ and confirm you will send OUR instructions, we will reserve the USD sweep account and flag for internal allocation on receipt.

Thanks,
Priyom

Alex / team — Rafael from Finance here. Confirming Redwood's operational position and proposed wording for the concession:

Policy summary (short):
- Standard stance: beneficiary receives full invoice amount; any intermediary/correspondent fees are sender's responsibility unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- Concession for this single consolidated sweep: Redwood will absorb intermediary/correspondent charges up to USD 30 per incoming wire for this invoice only. If fees exceed USD 30, the excess will be deducted from the paid invoice amount and shown as a "bank-charge adjustment" on the ledger.

Required acceptance language for Northbridge (please paste into treasury instruction email and reply to this thread):
"Northbridge Treasury confirms payment of Invoice #4207 via single USD sweep to Redwood's USD collection account (ref: NB-4207 | NB-TREASURY-REF-<X>). Northbridge requests Redwood to absorb intermediary/correspondent bank charges up to USD 30 for this incoming wire. Any charges above USD 30 may be netted against Invoice #4207. Northbridge will attempt to instruct OUR ordering to minimize beneficiary-side deductions."

VAT note: for EU/UK VAT we require either direct payment to the local legal entity (Option B) or submission of VAT registration and reclaim policy documents if you want Redwood to post reclaim entries on consolidated payment. If you intend to reclaim VAT yourselves, please confirm VAT IDs for the relevant entities.

Banking technical note (for treasury):
- Beneficiary: Redwood Inference, Redwood USD Collection Account
- Beneficiary account: 123456789 (US)
- Beneficiary bank: FirstRegional Bank
- Expected correspondent chain: FirstRegional -> GlobalCorr Bank (SWIFT: GCORUS33) -> Final Beneficiary Bank
- Please include the remittance reference exactly as: NB-4207 | NB-TREASURY-REF-<yourref>

We will populate the finance acceptance letter and sign once we receive Northbridge's confirmation text above.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Manager, Finance Operations — Redwood Inference
